title: Trump: The Council for National Policy organizes anti-lockdown protests & national COVID response
description_short: Trump: The Council for National Policy organizes anti-lockdown protests & national COVID response
description_medium: A TrumpFile timeline says the Council for National Policy helped organize anti-lockdown protests, with an early Pennsylvania event on April 20, 2020. It also says a CNP task force chaired by economist Art Laffer was involved in the Trump administration’s pandemic response. The account names partner groups and campaign aims, but does not document protest attendance or show that the protests changed state policy.
description_long: The Council for National Policy’s response to state COVID-19 restrictions was described in an April 2020 TrumpFile timeline. It identified an April 20 protest in Pennsylvania as the first known demonstration and said CNP worked with groups including FreedomWorks, the Heritage Foundation, Convention of States Action and Eagle Forum to promote events such as “ReOpen PA” and “ReOpen America.” The page also described a CNP initiative, the Save Our Country Task Force, as directing parts of the Trump administration’s pandemic response from early April. Economist Art Laffer chaired the task force; the source noted that Trump had awarded him the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2019. The timeline characterized the group’s broader 2020 activity as an effort to support Trump’s reelection, including anti-lockdown protests and public messaging about COVID-19. These are claims made by the linked timeline. It does not give attendance figures, identify the organizers of the Pennsylvania protest, or show that CNP’s activity caused a state to change restrictions. The entry documents the group’s reported political and pandemic-response activity, not a measured effect on public-health policy.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: The Council for National Policy organizes anti-lockdown protests & national COVID response
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: The Council for National Policy organizes anti-lockdown protests & national COVID response

notes: Read the linked timeline. The description attributes its claims about protest coordination and the task force to that source and does not state that the reported activity changed public-health restrictions.

title: Trump: Secret CNP / ALEC group meets with lawmakers from 20+ states to discuss election
description_short: Trump: Secret CNP / ALEC group meets with lawmakers from 20+ states to discuss election
description_medium: The Council for National Policy and American Legislative Exchange Council’s Political Process Working Group met on July 16, 2020, with lawmakers and election experts from at least 20 states, according to the linked timeline. Formed in August 2019, the group said its purpose was to influence the election in Trump’s favor. The source also describes earlier meetings about challenging results and voting rules.
description_long: The linked TrumpFile timeline reports that the Political Process Working Group, associated with the Council for National Policy and the American Legislative Exchange Council, met with lawmakers and election experts from at least 20 states on July 16, 2020. It says the group was established in August 2019 to influence the 2020 election in Donald Trump’s favor. The same account describes a December meeting about challenging election results and state policies that made voting easier, and a February meeting at a CNP conference where ALEC chief executive Lisa Nelson said she was working with attorneys to question the validity of election results. The source does not identify everyone who attended the July meeting or provide its agenda, decisions or follow-up actions. It also says the group’s total number of meetings was unclear. The reporting supports describing an organized election-policy effort and its stated aim; it does not by itself establish that the group changed election procedures, engaged in unlawful conduct or affected the result. Any account of those consequences would require the meeting records and evidence of subsequent implementation.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Secret CNP / ALEC group meets with lawmakers from 20+ states to discuss election
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Secret CNP / ALEC group meets with lawmakers from 20+ states to discuss election

notes: Read the linked timeline. It provides the group’s stated purpose, meeting dates and reported topics; the description does not assert that the group altered election rules or outcomes.

title: Summer Zervos Sexual Assault and Apprentice Exploitation
description_short: Summer Zervos Sexual Assault and Apprentice Exploitation
description_medium: Summer Zervos, a former Apprentice contestant, alleged that Donald Trump kissed and groped her without consent during encounters in 2007 and 2008. Trump denied the allegations and called her a liar. In a defamation lawsuit, Zervos’s lawyers cited calendar entries and phone records showing contact around the period; those records were evidence of contact, not an adjudicated finding of assault.
description_long: Summer Zervos, a former contestant on The Apprentice, alleged that Donald Trump kissed and groped her without consent during encounters in late 2007 and early 2008. Trump denied the allegations, saying he had not met her at a hotel or greeted her inappropriately, and later called her a liar. Zervos sued him for defamation after he publicly denied her account. In a 2019 court filing, her lawyer Mariann Wang cited emails, calendar entries and phone records to support Zervos’s account. The records showed that Trump had made multiple calls to Zervos during a three-month period around the time of the alleged encounters; her attorney argued that the contact supported her claims. The filings also said Zervos had sought legal advice in 2011 and contacted Fox News in 2015, before publicly accusing Trump in 2016. These records document contact and the chronology of Zervos’s complaints, but they are not themselves a court finding that an assault occurred. The account should therefore distinguish her allegations, Trump’s denial and the evidence presented in the defamation case.

preserved_fields.title: Summer Zervos Sexual Assault and Apprentice Exploitation
preserved_fields.description_short: Summer Zervos Sexual Assault and Apprentice Exploitation

notes: The linked CNN and ABC reports describe allegations, denial and records cited by Zervos’s attorneys. The records establish contact, not an adjudicated finding of assault; the wording maintains that distinction.

title: Trump: Steve Bannon caught using Facebook to push election lies to 2.45 million followers
description_short: Trump: Steve Bannon caught using Facebook to push election lies to 2.45 million followers
description_medium: Facebook removed seven pages operated by Steve Bannon that together had more than 2.45 million followers, according to the supplied report. The company said it removed clusters for coordinated inauthentic behavior; the pages posted claims about voter fraud and the election results. Bannon, a former Trump strategist, was associated with the pages, but the follower total does not show how many people saw or believed the posts.
description_long: On November 9, 2020, Facebook announced that it had removed seven pages associated with Steve Bannon, a former strategist for Donald Trump. The pages had a combined following of more than 2.45 million, according to the supplied report. Facebook said it had removed clusters of activity for using “inauthentic behavior tactics.” The pages were also reported to have posted claims about voter fraud, “illegal votes” and the election results. The action came after the presidential election, as false claims about vote counting and the outcome circulated online. The combined follower count describes the potential reach of the pages, not a verified number of unique viewers or people persuaded by their posts. Facebook’s explanation concerns its platform rules and account behavior; the packet does not include a full investigation of who created each page, how the audience was built or the specific reach of each post. The event documents a platform removal and the company’s stated rationale. It does not establish that Bannon directed every post or that the pages changed votes or the election result.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Steve Bannon caught using Facebook to push election lies to 2.45 million followers
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Steve Bannon caught using Facebook to push election lies to 2.45 million followers

notes: The Washington Post page timed out during this review. The description uses the supplied account of Facebook’s removal and rationale, avoids the unsupported label “criminal,” and does not treat page followers as unique reach or proof of changed votes.
proposed_correction: Use “associated with Facebook pages removed for coordinated inauthentic behavior” unless reporting establishes Bannon’s operational role in each page and post.

title: Trump: Mike Pompeo confirms that Russia is ‘pretty clearly' behind cyber espionage
description_short: Trump: Mike Pompeo confirms that Russia is ‘pretty clearly' behind cyber espionage
description_medium: Secretary of State Mike Pompeo said on December 18, 2020, that Russia was “pretty clearly” behind the SolarWinds cyberattack. He described a significant effort using third-party software to enter government systems and said investigators were still determining its scope. His statement was the administration’s strongest public attribution at that point, while acknowledging that details remained unresolved or classified.
description_long: On December 18, 2020, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo publicly attributed the SolarWinds cyber espionage campaign to Russia, saying it was “pretty clearly” responsible. He described the operation as a significant effort that used third-party software to place code in U.S. government systems and said it appeared to have reached private companies and governments in other countries as well. Pompeo told the Mark Levin Show that investigators were still unpacking the incident and that some details would likely remain classified. NPR reported that high-ranking Trump administration officials had said little publicly during the week after the breach became known, making Pompeo the most prominent official to assign responsibility at that time. President Trump had not mentioned the suspected attack for nearly a week and later suggested the media had exaggerated its scale, while appearing to question Russia’s role. Pompeo’s remarks were an official public attribution, not a complete technical account of the breach or its scope. The statement made the administration’s position clearer while the investigation and response were still developing.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Mike Pompeo confirms that Russia is ‘pretty clearly' behind cyber espionage
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Mike Pompeo confirms that Russia is ‘pretty clearly' behind cyber espionage

notes: Read the linked NPR report. It supports Pompeo’s public attribution and the software compromise description; the account distinguishes his attribution from a complete technical assessment.
